title: Glasshouse — institutional accountability evidence dataset (say vs. do)
description:
Glasshouse is a public, machine-readable record of what large asset managers say about how they vote their funds' shares (archived proxy-voting and stewardship policies, with dates) and how those funds actually voted (SEC Form N-PX), with 13-F holdings and a public enforcement record alongside.

This version holds 24,034,092 fund vote lines from SEC Form N-PX filings for the voting years July 2023 to June 2026, filed by fund trusts of 37 financial institutions. For 34 of them (BlackRock, Dimensional, Vanguard, State Street, Fidelity, American Century, Nuveen/TIAA, PGIM, Thrivent, Victory Capital, Principal, First Trust, Dodge & Cox, Capital Group, Columbia Threadneedle, Northern Trust, MFS, Morgan Stanley, Franklin Templeton including Putnam, AllianceBernstein, Wellington, Federated Hermes, Goldman Sachs, Allspring, J.P. Morgan, Parametric, Janus Henderson, Neuberger Berman, Invesco, Lord Abbett, Charles Schwab, DWS, T. Rowe Price, BNY) every kind of vote is on file for the fund trusts held; for UBS, BNP Paribas and Bank of America only executive-pay (say-on-pay) votes are on file. The fund trusts held are often a small part of a large manager: this is not a complete record of any manager's voting. Some 2025–2026 Dimensional N-PX exhibits contain exactly 500,000 proxy records in the SEC file itself and appear capped, so their counts are lower bounds. It also holds 263 dated versions of 35 managers' policy documents (hashes, dates and archive links; no policy text), 580,106 13-F holding rows and 14,887 enforcement actions.

Corrections. Versions 2026-11-18.3, 2026-11-19 and 2026-11-19.2 counted 290 Morgan Stanley vote lines twice (one ETF trust's 2025 votes, restated by an amended N-PX/A with different share counts; about 0.001% of their votes). In this version a vote line restated by a later N-PX/A of the same filer and period is superseded by it. Earlier, versions 2026-11-17.2, 2026-11-17.3, 2026-11-18 and 2026-11-18.2 shipped repeated N-PX vote lines as distinct votes (0.62–0.69% of their votes; mostly Dimensional, whose line counts there are about 3% too high). This version is corrected: no shipped vote is a marked duplicate, and the build now refuses to run when duplicate flags are stale. Per-release counts: https://github.com/glasshouse-records/promises-kept-or-not/blob/main/docs/CORRECTIONS.md

New in this version: First Trust (10 ETF and open-end trusts with votes) and Dodge & Cox fund registrants (about 640,000 vote lines), each keyed to its voting adviser from the funds' own SAIs. First Trust's SAIs said until 2022–2023 that First Trust had adopted the ISS Proxy Voting Guidelines and from then on attach First Trust's own Proxy Voting Guidelines, so its funds' votes carry the key FIRST_TRUST only from that change (the ISS guidelines themselves are not archived); series whose own SAI delegates voting to a sub-adviser are keyed EXTERNAL. Dodge & Cox's policy is archived from its website and from the funds' SAIs (one edition a year, 2021–2026).

Votes are attributed to the adviser that cast them, not the brand: where one group's funds are voted by different advisers under different policies every vote carries an adviser_key, and a policy may only be compared with votes of the same key. Three derived tables give one row per manager per ballot item (shareholder proposals, director elections, say-on-pay). Every column and code is defined in DATASHEET.md; coverage and known gaps are stated in COVERAGE.json; every file is checksummed in MANIFEST.sha256.

Code: https://github.com/glasshouse-records/promises-kept-or-not (MIT). The DATASHEET records the exact code commit that built these files.

The dataset records facts from public filings. It makes no finding of wrongdoing about anyone.
notes: Code: MIT. Data: CC-BY-4.0. Built from code commit recorded in DATASHEET.md.
